paragraphs.text: "If these sensors are working . . . we're on the other side of the Galaxy." —Ensign Harry Kim
"We all joined Starfleet to dive headfirst into the unknown."
"If we're going to be damned, let's be damned for what we really are." —Captain Jean-Luc Picard
The DOT-7s are designed to make repairs in any conditions too dangerous for humanoids.
"Damn. Where are the calluses we doctors are supposed to grow over our feelings?"
The EMH Mark 1 distills thousands of medical references and the experiences of forty-seven medical officers into a single unit, though its bedside manner leaves much to be desired.
"Stop whining. Sto-Vo-Kor will be there later."
"Resistance is *not* futile."
"The holodeck safeties are still engaged, right?" —Ensign Kei
"I have the utmost confidence in your ability to perform the impossible."
"I don't believe this was a fair test of my command abilities."
Deflector shields use intense graviton fields to create a "solid" surface from nothing at all.
Although she was a Kelpien, a prey species, she feared no predator once behind the controls.
"Kouassi to bridge. Captain, the intruders look like Starfleet, but their combadge is different. It's . . . a dagger through a planet?"
"She has an illusion, and you have reality. May you find your way as pleasant." —The Keeper, magistrate of Talos IV
"You're too late. We are everywhere."
The ionized gasses of the Mutara Nebula wreaked havoc with sensors and shielding.
For the briefest of moments, Spock felt fear. Not of the rabbit, but that the universe could let it exist without logical cause.
"Whatever they say, you have to respond in kind. Otherwise they'll take offense."
George and Gracie escaped extinction, and in the process, saved Earth.
"Okay, new plan!"
Some gestures are universal.
"We have analyzed your defensive capabilities as being unable to withstand us. If you defend yourselves, you will be punished." —The Borg
Peace through superior firepower. —Minosian motto, pre-extinction
"Your tongue is as sharp as a warrior's! Let's see if your blade is as well!"
"I will rest when my blade knows vengeance."
Klingons who challenge the High Council are denied the right of personal combat. They must select a second—a *cha'DIch*—to defend them.
"You will be assimilated."
"Be honest, Captain. Warrior to warrior. You do prefer it this way, don't you? As it was meant to be. No peace in our time."
There are no old warriors. —Klingon proverb
"How can we be powerful enough to wipe out a planet and still be so helpless?" —Dr. Leonard McCoy
"Consensus achieved. Disseminating."
"From this time forward, you will service us." —Locutus of Borg
The Vau N'Akat created the Watchers to observe and the Drednoks to enforce.
After the collapse of their civilization, the people of M-113 became little more than predators, but they never abandoned their need for love.
"Are you the best crew in the fleet or not?!"
Starfleet tactical training demands cadets learn how to handle any situation—even failure.
Before miners discovered the Horta on Janus VI, silicon-based life was considered little more than science fiction.
"I've done far worse than kill you. I've hurt you, and I wish to go on hurting you." —Khan Noonien Singh
"Lesson six of security: know when to bend the rules."
"What is the point of your spikes?" asked the *boqrat*. "You cannot attack with them." "Perhaps not," laughed the *targ*. "But they bring me great joy!"
Some knowledge is lost. Some knowledge is buried.
"Away team to *Enterprise*. No life signs anywhere. It's as if the entire colony simply walked away."
"Fire in engineering! Response teams, move!"
Fortune favors the bold. —Human proverb
The Tholian Assembly does not suffer trespassers lightly.
"So be it, human. We shall work together, if only so I can be the one to kill you."
The loyal Vorta saw to the distribution of ketracel-white, the Dominion's powerful combination of narcotics and life-giving enzymes.
Interspecies diplomacy isn't a calling for the faint of heart.
"Dammit, Jim. We've been over this!" —Dr. Leonard McCoy

"The moopsy is a small mammal known for its endearing appearance. The creature's diet consists of living bone tissue, which it liquefies and drinks via a process witnesses describe as 'upsettingly swift and graphic.'" —*Lawmim Galactopedia*
Despite their terrifying appearance, mugato are loving, social creatures who form strong family bonds, even mourning fallen family members.
The Voth are one of the Galaxy's oldest spacefaring species.
Before the Cardassian occupation, Bajor was a center of culture and learning.
"The Orion Syndicate. An alliance of all the worst smugglers, pirates, and general malfeasants you'd cross two streets to avoid." —Constable Odo
"Electromagnetic stimulation triggers bioluminescence and causes a 22% increase in aesthetic appeal. But to what end?"
Six sapient species evolved in parallel on Xindus. They learned to turn their differences into strengths . . . but only after civil war reduced their number to five.
"I am no longer Borg, but the prospect of becoming human is . . . unsettling. I don't know where I belong."
What Airiam lost made what she kept so much more precious.
The hellish mines of Remus fueled the war efforts of the Romulan Star Empire, until the Remans found a champion.
In the milky pools permeating the caves of Mak'ala, Trill symbionts await their new lives.
After Gul Dukat aligned the Cardassian Union with the Dominion, the Founders moved their military headquarters to Cardassia Prime to better oversee war efforts.
The metaphasic radiation of the Ba'ku planet promised medical marvels, as long as the locals could be quietly removed.
The Zakdorn run Surplus Depot Zed-15, salvaging decommissioned ships to supply future Federation projects.
Sooner or later, every Starfleet vessel passes through Spacedock, whether for resupply, repairs, or complete retrofit.
As one of the Galaxy's few ectothermic sapient species, Cardassians prefer high temperatures. Many use sweltering saunas to "charge" themselves before interacting with other species.
"Neural's active mantle and energetic water cycle create staggeringly beautiful rock formations and a variety of tropical microclimates. Don't feed the wildlife." —*Lawmim Galactopedia*
The Edo view their homeworld as a paradise, though outsiders find their strict justice system senselessly brutal.
Earth's restored cetacean population eventually came to see the wreck of the *Bounty* as a sort of holy site.
"Ironic, isn't it? That something so unique could care so little for the diversity of life." —Captain Jean-Luc Picard
